19.23: Then Jesus sayd unto his disciples, Verely I say unto you, that a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.
19.24: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, then for a rich man to enter into ye kingdom of God.
19.25: And whe his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amased, saying, Who then can be saved?
19.26: And Jesus beheld them, and sayde unto them, With men this is vnpossible, but with God all things are possible.
19.27: Then answered Peter, and said to him, Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee: what therefore shall we have?
19.28: And Jesus said unto them, Verely I say to you, that when the Sonne of man shall sit in the throne of his maiestie, ye which folowed me in the regeneration, shall sit also upon twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
19.29: And whosoever shall forsake houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my Names sake, he shall receive an hundreth fold more, and shall inherit everlasting life.
19.30: But many that are first, shalbe last, and the last shalbe first.

20.1: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain, housholder, which went out at the dawning of the day to hire labourers into his vineyard.
20.2: And he agreed with the labourers for a peny a day, and sent them into his vineyard.
20.3: And he went out about the third hour, and saw other standing idle in the market place,
20.4: And sayd unto them, Goe ye also into my vineyard, and whatsoever is right, I will give you: and they went their way.
20.5: Again he went out about the sixt and ninth hour, and did likewise.
20.6: And he went about the eleventh hour, and found other standing idle, and sayd unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
20.7: They sayd unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He sayd to them, Goe ye also into my vineyard, and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.
20.8: And when even was come, the master of the vineyard sayd unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning at the last, till thou come to the first.
20.9: And they which were hired about ye eleventh hour, came and received every man a penie.
20.10: Now when the first came, they supposed that they should receive more, but they likewise received every man a penie.
20.11: And when they had received it, they murmured against the master of the house,
20.12: Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.
20.13: And hee answered one of them, saying, Friend, I doe thee no wrong: didst thou not agree with me for a penie?
20.14: Take that which is thine own, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, as much as to thee.
20.15: Is it not lawful for me to do as I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?
20.16: So the last shalbe first, and the first last: for many are called, but few chosen.
20.17: And Jesus went up to Hierusalem, and took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
20.18: Behold, wee goe up to Hierusalem, and the Sonne of man shall bee delivered unto the chief priestes, and unto the Scribes, and they shall condemn him to death,
20.19: And shall deliver him to the Gentiles, to mock, and to scourge, and to crucifie him, but the third day he shall rise again.
20.20: Then came to him the mother of Zebedeus children with her sonnes, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
20.21: And he said unto her, What wouldest thou? She said to him, Graunt that these my two sonnes may sit, the one at thy right hand, and the other at thy left hand in thy kingdom.
20.22: And Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I shalbe baptized with? They said to him, We are able.
20.23: And he said unto them, Ye shall drink in deed of my cup, and shall be baptized with the baptism, that I am baptized with, but to sit at my right hand, and at my left hand, is not mine to give: but it shalbe given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.
20.24: And when the other ten heard this, they disdained at the two brethren.
20.25: Therefore Jesus called them unto him, and said, We know that the lordes of the Gentiles have domination over them, and they that are great, exercise authoritie over them.
20.26: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your servant.
20.27: And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant.
20.28: Even as the Sonne of man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life for the ransom of many.
20.29: And as they departed from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
20.30: And behold, two blind men, sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus passed by, cryed, saying, O Lord, the Sonne of David, have mercie on us.
20.31: And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, O Lord, the Sonne of David, have mercie on us.
20.32: Then Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I should do to you?
20.33: They said to him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
20.34: And Jesus mooued with compassion, touched their eyes, and immediatly their eyes received sight, and they followed him.

21.1: And when they drew neere to Hierusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of the Olives, then sent Jesus two disciples,
21.2: Saying to them, Goe into the town that is over against you, and anon yee shall find an ass bound, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.
21.3: And if any man say ought unto you, say ye, that the Lord hath need of them, and straightway he will let them goe.
21.4: All this was done that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken by the Prophet, saying,
21.5: Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek and sitting upon an ass, and a colt, the foal of an ass used to the yoke.
21.6: So the disciples went, and did as Jesus had commanded them,
21.7: And brought the ass and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and set him thereon.
21.8: And a great multitude spred their garments in the way: and other cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.
21.9: Moreover, the people that went before, and they also that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Sonne of David, Blessed be hee that cometh in the Name of the Lord, Hosanna thou which art in the highest heavens.
21.10: And when he was come into Hierusalem, all the citie was mooued, saying, Who is this?
21.11: And the people said, This is Jesus that Prophet of Nazareth in Galile.
21.12: And Jesus went into the Temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the Temple, and overthrew the tables of the money chagers, and the seates of them that sold doves,
21.13: And said to them, it is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer: but ye have made it a denne of theeues.
21.14: Then the blind, and the halt came to him in the Temple, and he healed them.
21.15: But when the chief priestes and Scribes saw the marueiles that hee did, and the children crying in the Temple, and saying, Hosanna to the Sonne of David, they disdained,
21.16: And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus said unto them, Yea: read ye never, By the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast made perfite the praise?
21.17: So hee left them, and went out of the citie unto Bethania, and lodged there.
21.18: And in the morning, as he returned into the citie, he was hungrie,
21.19: And seeing a figge tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves onely, and said to it, Never fruit grow on thee henceforwards. And anon the figge tree withered.
21.20: And when his disciples saw it, they marueiled, saying, How soon is the figge tree withered!
21.21: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Verely I say unto you, if ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only doe that, which I have done to the figge tree, but also if ye say unto this mountain, Take thy self away, and cast thy self into the sea, it shalbe done.
21.22: And whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, if ye beleeue, ye shall receive it.
21.23: And whe he was come into the Temple, the chief Priestes, and the Elders of the people came unto him, as he was teaching, and said, By what authoritie doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authoritie?
21.24: Then Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask of you a certain thing, which if ye tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authoritie I doe these things.
21.25: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men? Then they reasoned among themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven, he will say unto us, Why did ye not then beleeue him?
21.26: And if we say, Of men, we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a Prophet.
21.27: Then they answered Jesus, and said, We can not tell. And he said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authoritie I doe these things.
21.28: But what think ye? A certain man had two sonnes, and came to the elder, and said, Sonne, goe and work to day in my vineyard.
21.29: But he answered, and said, I will not: yet afterward he repented himself, and went.
21.30: Then came he to the second, and said likewise. And he answered, and said, I will, Syr: yet he went not.
21.31: Whether of them twain did the will of the father? They said unto him, The first. Jesus said unto them, Verely I say unto you, that the Publicanes and the harlots goe before you into the kingdom of God.
21.32: For John came unto you in the way of righteousnes, and yee beleeued him not: but the Publicanes, and the harlots beleeued him, and ye, though ye saw it, were not mooued with repentance afterward, that ye might beleeue him.
21.33: Hear another parable, There was a certain housholder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and made a winepress therein, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a strange countrey.
21.34: And when the time of the fruit drew neere, hee sent his servants to the husbandmen to receive the fruites thereof.
21.35: And ye husbandmen took his servants and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
21.36: Again hee sent other servants, moe then the first: and they did the like unto them.
21.37: But last of all he sent unto them his own sonne, saying, They will reverence my sonne.
21.38: But when the husbandmen saw the sonne, they said among themselves, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, and let us take his inheritance.
21.39: So they took him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
21.40: When therefore the Lord of the vineyard shall come, what will hee doe to those husbandmen?
21.41: They said unto him, Hee will cruelly destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall deliver him the fruites in their seasons.
21.42: Jesus said unto them, Read ye never in the Scriptures, The stone which the builders refused, the same is made the head of the corner? This was the Lordes doing, and it is marueilous in our eyes.
21.43: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shalbe taken from you, and shalbe given to a nation, which shall bring foorth the fruites thereof.
21.44: And whosoever shall fall on this stone, he shalbe broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will dash him a pieces.
21.45: And when the chief Priestes and Pharises had heard his parables, they perceived that hee spake of them.
21.46: And they seeking to lay handes on him, feared the people, because they took him as a Prophet.

22.1: Then Jesus answered, and spake unto them again in parables, saying,
22.2: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain King which maried his sonne,
22.3: And sent foorth his servants, to call them that were bidde to the wedding, but they would not come.
22.4: Again hee sent foorth other servants, saying. Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: mine oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all thinges are readie: come unto the mariage.
22.5: But they made light of it, and went their wayes, one to his farm, and another about his marchandise.
22.6: And the remnant took his servants, and intreated them sharpely, and slew them.
22.7: But when the King heard it, he was wroth, and sent foorth his warriers, and destroyed those murtherers, and burnt up their citie.
22.8: Then said hee to his servants, Truely the wedding is prepared: but they which were bidden, were not worthy.
22.9: Go ye therefore out into the high wayes, and as many as ye find, bid them to the mariage.
22.10: So those seruantes went out into the hie wayes, and gathered together all that ever they found, both good and bad: so the wedding was furnished with ghestes.
22.11: Then the King came in, to see the ghestes, and saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment.
22.12: And he sayd unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither, and hast not on a wedding garment? And he was speachlesse.
22.13: Then sayd the King to the servants, Bind him hand and foot: take him away, and cast him into utter darkenes: there shalbe weeping and gnashing of teeth.
22.14: For many are called, but few chosen.
22.15: Then went the Pharises and took counsel how they might tangle him in talk.
22.16: And they sent unto him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Master, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God truely, neither carest for any man: for thou considerest not the person of men.
22.17: Tell us therefore, how thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?
22.18: But Jesus perceived their wickednes, and sayd, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?
22.19: Shew me the tribute money. And they brought him a peny.
22.20: And he sayde unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?
22.21: They sayd unto him, Cesars. Then sayd he unto them, Give therefore to Cesar, the things which are Cesars, and give unto God, those things which are Gods.
22.22: And when they heard it, they marueiled, and left him, and went their way.
22.23: The same day the Sadduces came to him (which say that there is no resurrection) and asked him,
22.24: Saying, Master, Moses sayd, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marie his wife by the right of alliance, and raise up seed unto his brother.
22.25: Now there were with us seven brethren, and the first maried a wife, and deceased: and having none yssue, left his wife unto his brother.
22.26: Likewise also the second, and the third, unto the seventh.
22.27: And last of all the woman died also.
22.28: Therefore in the resurrection, whose wife shall she be of the seven? for all had her.
22.29: Then Jesus answered, and sayd unto them, Ye are deceived, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
22.30: For in the resurrection they neither marie wives, nor wives are bestowed in mariage, but are as the Angels of God in heaven.
22.31: And concerning the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read what is spoken vuto you of God, saying,
22.32: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
22.33: And when the multitude heard it, they were astonied at his doctrine.
22.34: But when the Pharises had heard, that he had put the Sadduces to silence, they assembled together.
22.35: And one of them, which was an expounder of the Law, asked him a question, tempting him, and saying,
22.36: Master, which is ye great commandement in the Law?
22.37: Jesus sayd to him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
22.38: This is the first and the great commandement.
22.39: And the second is like unto this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thy self.
22.40: On these two commandements hangeth the whole Law, and the Prophets.
22.41: While the Pharises were gathered together, Jesus asked them,
22.42: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose sonne is he? They sayd unto him, Dauids.
22.43: He sayd unto them, How then doeth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,
22.44: The Lord sayd to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footestoole?
22.45: If then David call him Lord, how is he his sonne?
22.46: And none could answer him a word, neither durst any from that day foorth ask him any moe questions.

23.1: Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples,
23.2: Saying, The Scribes and the Pharises sit in Moses seat.
23.3: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and doe: but after their workes doe not: for they say, and doe not.
23.4: For they bind heauie burdens, and grieuous to be borne, and lay them on mens shoulders, but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
23.5: All their workes they doe for to be seen of men: for they make their phylacteries broad, and make long the frindges of their garments,
23.6: And love the chief place at feastes, and to have the chief seates in the assemblies,
23.7: And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
23.8: But be not ye called, Rabbi: for one is your doctour, to wit, Christ, and all ye are brethren.
23.9: And call no man your father upon the earth: for there is but one, your father which is in heaven.
23.10: Be not called doctours: for one is your doctour, even Christ.
23.11: But he that is greatest among you, let him be your servant.
23.12: For whosoever will exalt himself, shall be brought low: and whosoever will humble himself, shalbe exalted.
23.13: Wo therefore be unto you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites, because ye shut up the kingdom of heaven before men: for ye your selves go not in, neither suffer ye them that would enter, to come in.
23.14: Wo be unto you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye deuoure widowes houses, even under a colour of long prayers: wherefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.
23.15: Wo be unto you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye compass sea and land to make one of your profession: and when he is made, ye make him two fold more the child of hell, then you your selves.
23.16: Wo be unto you blind guides, which say, Whosoever sweareth by the Temple, it is nothing: but whosoever sweareth by the gold of the Temple, he offendeth.
23.17: Ye fooles and blind, whether is greater, the gold, or the Temple that sanctifieth the gold?
23.18: And whosoever sweareth by the altar, it is nothing: but whosoever sweareth by the offering that is upon it, offendeth.
23.19: Ye fooles and blind, whether is greater, the offering, or the altar which sanctifieth the offering?
23.20: Whosoever therefore sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon.
23.21: And whosoever sweareth by the Temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.
23.22: And he that sweareth by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.
23.23: Wo be to you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye tithe mynt, and annyse, and cummyn, and leave the weightier matters of the law, as iudgement, and mercy and fidelitie. These ought ye to have done, and not to have left the other.
23.24: Ye blind guides, which strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel.
23.25: Wo be to you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye make clean the utter side of the cup, and of the platter: but within they are ful of briberie and excess.
23.26: Thou blind Pharise, cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.
23.27: Wo be to you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye are like unto whited tombes, which appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead mens bones, and all filthines.
23.28: So are ye also: for outward ye appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisie and iniquitie.
23.29: Wo be unto you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye build the tombes of the Prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
23.30: And say, If we had been in the dayes of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the Prophets.
23.31: So then ye be witnesses unto your selves, that ye are the children of them that murthered the Prophets.
23.32: Fulfil ye also ye measure of your fathers.
23.33: O serpents, the generation of vipers, how should ye escape the damnation of hell!
23.34: Wherefore behold, I send unto you Prophets, and wise men, and Scribes, and of them ye shall kill and crucifie: and of them shall ye scourge in your Synagogues, and persecute from citie to citie,
23.35: That upon you may come all the righteous blood that was shed upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous, unto the blood of Zacharias the sonne of Barachias, whom ye slew between the Temple and the altar.
23.36: Verely I say unto you, all these things shall come upon this generation.
23.37: Hierusalem, Hierusalem, which killest the Prophets, and stonest them which are sent to thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, as the henne gathereth her chickins under her wings, and ye would not!
23.38: Behold, your habitation shalbe left unto you desolate,
23.39: For I say unto you, ye shall not see mee henceforth till that ye say, Blessed is he that cometh in the Name of the Lord.

24.1: And Jesus went out, and departed from the Temple, and his disciples came to him, to shew him the building of the Temple.
24.2: And Jesus sayd unto them, See ye not all these things? Verely I say unto you, there shall not be here left a stone upon a stone, that shall not be cast down.
24.3: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, his disciples came unto him apart, saying, Tell us when these things shall be, and what sign shalbe of thy coming, and of the end of the world.
24.4: And Jesus answered, and sayd unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you.
24.5: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ, and shall deceive many.
24.6: And ye shall hear of wars, and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
24.7: For nation shall rise against nation, and realm against realm, and there shalbe famine, and pestilence, and earthquakes in divers places.
24.8: All these are but ye beginning of sorowes.
24.9: Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you, and ye shall be hated of all nations for my Names sake.
24.10: And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.
24.11: And many false prophets shall arise, and shall deceive many.
24.12: And because iniquitie shalbe increased, the love of many shalbe cold.
24.13: But he that endureth to the end, he shalbe saved.
24.14: And this Gospel of the kingdom shalbe preached through the whole world for a witnes unto all nations, and then shall the end come.
24.15: When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, set in the holy place (let him that readeth consider it.)
24.16: Then let them which be in Judea, flee into the mountaines.
24.17: Let him which is on the house top, not come down to fetch any thing out of his house.
24.18: And he that is in the field, let not him return back to fetch his clothes.
24.19: And woe shalbe to them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those dayes.
24.20: But pray that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the Sabbath day.
24.21: For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not from the beginning of the world to this time, nor shalbe.
24.22: And except those dayes should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elects sake those dayes shalbe shortened.
24.23: Then if any shall say unto you, Loe, here is Christ, or there, beleeue it not.
24.24: For there shall arise false Christes, and false prophets, and shall shew great signes and wonders, so that if it were possible, they should deceive the very elect.
24.25: Behold, I have told you before.
24.26: Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert, goe not forth: Behold, he is in the secret places, beleeue it not.
24.27: For as the lightning cometh out of the East, and is seen into the West, so shall also the coming of the Sonne of man be.
24.28: For wheresoever a dead carkeis is, thither will the Egles be gathered together.
24.29: And immediatly after ye tribulations of those dayes, shall the sunne be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the starres shall fal from heaven, and ye powers of heave shalbe shake.
24.30: And then shall appear the sign of the Sonne of man in heaven: and then shall all the kinreds of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Sonne of man come in the cloudes of heaven with power and great glorie.
24.31: And he shall send his Angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect, from the four windes, and from the one end of the heavens unto the other.
24.32: Now learn the parable of the figge tree: when her bough is yet tender, and it putteth foorth leaves, ye know that sommer is neere.
24.33: So likewise ye, when ye see all these things, know that the kingdom of God is neere, eve at ye doores.
24.34: Verely I say unto you, this generation shall not pass, till all these things be done.
24.35: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my wordes shall not pass away.
24.36: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no not the Angels of heaven, but my father only.
24.37: But as the dayes of Noe were, so likewise shall the coming of the Sonne of man be.
24.38: For as in the dayes before the flood, they did eat and drink, marrie, and give in mariage, unto the day that Noe entred into the Ark,
24.39: And knew nothing, till the flood came, and took them all away, so shall also the coming of the Sonne of man be.
24.40: Then two shall be in the fieldes, the one shalbe received, and the other shalbe refused.
24.41: Two women shalbe grinding at ye mill: the one shalbe received, and the other shalbe refused.
24.42: Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your master will come.
24.43: Of this be sure, that if the good man of the house knew at what watch the thief would come, he would surely watch, and not suffer his house to be digged through.
24.44: Therefore be ye also ready: for in the hour that ye think not, will the Sonne of man come.
24.45: Who then is a faithful seruaunt and wise, whom his master hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in season?
24.46: Blessed is that servant, whom his master when he cometh, shall find so doing.
24.47: Verely I say unto you, he shall make him ruler over all his goods.
24.48: But if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My master doth deferre his coming,
24.49: And begin to smite his fellowes, and to eat, and to drink with the drunken,
24.50: That seruaunts master will come in a day, when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not ware of,
24.51: And will cut him off, and give him his portion with hypocrites: there shalbe weeping, and gnashing of teeth.

25.1: Then the kingdom of heaven shalbe likened unto tenne virgins, which took their lampes, and went foorth to meet the bridegrome.
25.2: And five of them were wise, and five foolish.
25.3: The foolish took their lampes, but took none oyle with them.
25.4: But the wise took oyle in their vessels with their lampes.
25.5: Now while the bridegrome taried long, all slumbred and slept.
25.6: And at midnight there was a crie made, Behold, the bridegrome cometh: goe out to meet him.
25.7: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lampes.
25.8: And the foolish said to the wise, Give us of your oyle, for our lampes are out.
25.9: But the wise answered, saying, Not so, lest there will not be ynough for us and you: but goe ye rather to them that sell, and bye for your selves.
25.10: And while they went to bye, the bridegrome came: and they that were readie, went in with him to the wedding, and the gate was shut.
25.11: Afterwards came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.
25.12: But he answered, and said, Verely I say unto you, I know you not.
25.13: Watch therfore: for ye know neither the day, nor the hour, when the sonne of man will come.
25.14: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man that going into a strange countrey, called his servants, and delivered to them his goods.
25.15: And unto one he gave five talents, and to an other two, and to another one, to every man after his own ability, and straightway went from home.
25.16: Then he that had received the five talents, went and occupied with them, and gained other five talents.
25.17: Likewise also, he that received two, he also gained other two.
25.18: But he that received that one, went and digged it in the earth, and hid his masters money.
25.19: But after a long season, the master of those servants came, and reckoned with them.
25.20: Then came he that had received five talents, and brought other five talents, saying, Master, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained with them other five talents.
25.21: Then his master said unto him, It is well done good servant and faithful, Thou hast been faithful in litle, I will make thee ruler over much: enter into thy masters joy.
25.22: Also he that had received two talents, came, and said, Master, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talets more.
25.23: His master said unto him, It is well done good servant, and faithful, Thou hast been faithful in litle, I will make thee ruler over much: enter into thy masters joy.
25.24: Then he which had received the one talent, came, and said, Master, I knew that thou wast an hard man, which reapest where thou sowedst not, and gatherest where thou strawedst not:
25.25: I was therefore afraid, and went, and hid thy talent in the earth: behold, thou hast thine own.
25.26: And his master answered, and said unto him, Thou evil servant, and slouthfull, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I strawed not.
25.27: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to ye exchangers, and then at my coming should I have received mine own with vantage.
25.28: Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath tenne talents.
25.29: For unto every man that hath, it shall be given, and he shall have abundance, and from him that hath not, even that he hath, shalbe taken away.
25.30: Cast therefore that unprofitable servant into utter darkenes: there shalbe weeping and gnashing of teeth.
25.31: And when the Sonne of man cometh in his glory, and all the holy Angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glorie,
25.32: And before him shalbe gathered all nations, and he shall seperate them one from another, as a shepheard separateth the sheep from ye goates.
25.33: And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, and the goates on the left.
25.34: Then shall ye king say to them on his right hand, Come ye blessed of my father: take the inheritance of the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
25.35: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I thirsted, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in unto you.
25.36: I was naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.
25.37: Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or a thirst, and gave thee drink?
25.38: And when saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in unto us? or naked, and clothed thee?
25.39: Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?
25.40: And the King shall answer, and say unto them, Verely I say unto you, in as much as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethre, ye have done it to me.
25.41: Then shall he say unto them on ye left hand, Depart from me ye cursed, into everlasting fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels.
25.42: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I thirsted, and ye gave me no drink:
25.43: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in unto you: I was naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.
25.44: Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or a thirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee?
25.45: Then shall he answer them, and say, Verely I say unto you, in as much as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.
25.46: And these shall goe into everlasting pain, and the righteous into life eternal.

26.1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said unto his disciples,
26.2: Ye know that after two dayes is ye Passeouer, and the Sonne of man shalbe delivered to be crucified.
26.3: Then assembled together the chief Priests, and the Scribes, and the Elders of ye people into the hall of the high Priest called Caiaphas:
26.4: And consulted together that they might take Jesus by subtiltie, and kill him.
26.5: But they sayd, Not on the feast day, least any vprore be among the people.
26.6: And when Jesus was in Bethania, in the house of Simon the leper,
26.7: There came unto him a woman, which had a box of very costly oyntment, and powred it on his head, as he sat at the table.
26.8: And when his disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, What needed this waste?
26.9: For this oyntment might have been sold for much, and been given to the poor.
26.10: And Jesus knowing it, sayde unto them, Why trouble yee the woman? for she hath wrought a good woorke upon me.
26.11: For yee have the poor alwayes with you, but me shall yee not have alwaies.
26.12: For in that she powred this oyntment on my bodie, she did it to burie me.
26.13: Verely I say unto you, wheresoever this Gospel shall bee preached throughout all the world, there shall also this that she hath done, be spoken of for a memorial of her.
26.14: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief Priestes,
26.15: And said, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? and they appoynted unto him thirtie pieces of silver.
26.16: And from that time, he sought opportunitie to betraie him.
26.17: Now on the first day of the feast of vnleauened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the Passeouer?
26.18: And he said, Goe yee into the citie to such a man, and say to him, The master saieth, My time is at hand: I will keep the Passeouer at thine house with my disciples.
26.19: And the disciples did as Jesus had given them charge, and made readie the Passeouer.
26.20: So when the Even was come, hee sat down with the twelve.
26.21: And as they did eat, he sayde, Verely I say unto you, that one of you shall betraie me.
26.22: And they were exceeding sorowfull, and began every one of them to say unto him, Is it I, Master?
26.23: And hee answered and sayde, Hee that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, hee shall betraie me.
26.24: Surely the Sonne of man goeth his way, as it is written of him: but woe be to that man, by whom the Sonne of man is betrayed: it had been good for that man, if hee had never been borne.
26.25: Then Judas which betraied him, answered and sayde, Is it I, Master? He sayde unto him, Thou hast sayd it.
26.26: And as they did eat, Jesus took the bread, and when he had blessed, he brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and sayd, Take, eat: this is my bodie.
26.27: Also he took the cuppe, and when he had given thankes, he gave it them, saying, Drink ye all of it.
26.28: For this is my blood of the New Testament, that is shedde for many, for the remission of sinnes.
26.29: I say unto you, that I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day, when I shall drink it new with you in my Fathers kingdom.
26.30: And when they had sung a Psalm, they went out into the mount of Olives.
26.31: Then said Jesus unto them, All yee shall be offended by me this night: for it is written, I wil smite the shepheard, and the sheep of the flock shalbe scattered.
26.32: But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galile.
26.33: But Peter aunswered, and sayde unto him, Though that al men should be offended by thee, yet will I never be offended.
26.34: Jesus sayde unto him, Verely I say unto thee, that this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt denie me thrise.
26.35: Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, I will in no case denie thee. Likewise also sayd all the disciples.
26.36: Then went Jesus with them into a place which is called Gethsemane, and said unto his disciples, Sit ye here, while I goe, and pray yonder.
26.37: And hee took unto him Peter, and the two sonnes of Zebedeus, and began to wax sorowfull, and grieuously troubled.
26.38: Then sayde Jesus unto them, My soul is very heauie, even unto the death: tarie yee here, and watch with me.
26.39: So hee went a litle further, and fell on his face, and praied, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt.
26.40: After, hee came unto the disciples, and found them a sleep, and sayde to Peter, What? could yee not watch with me one hour?
26.41: Watch, and praie, that yee enter not into tentation: the spirit in deed is readie, but the flesh is weak.
26.42: Again he went away the second time, and praied, saying, O my Father, if this cuppe can not pass away from mee, but that I must drink it, thy will be done.
26.43: And he came, and found them a sleep again, for their eyes were heauie.
26.44: So he left them and went away again, and praied the third time, saying the same woordes.
26.45: Then came he to his disciples, and said unto them, Sleep henceforth, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Sonne of man is given into the hands of sinners.
26.46: Rise, let us goe: behold, hee is at hand that betraieth me.
26.47: And while hee yet spake, loe Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swordes and staves, from the high Priests and Elders of the people.
26.48: Now he that betraied him, had given them a token, saying, Whomesoeuer I shall kiss, that is he, laie hold on him.
26.49: And forthwith he came to Jesus, and sayd, God save thee, Master, and kissed him.
26.50: Then Jesus sayde unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
26.51: And behold, one of them which were with Jesus, stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and strooke a seruaunt of the high Priest, and smote off his ear.
26.52: Then sayde Jesus unto him, Put up thy sword into his place: for all that take the sword, shall perish with the sword.
26.53: Either thinkest thou, that I can not now pray to my Father, and he will give me moe then twelve legions of Angels?
26.54: How then should the Scriptures bee fulfilled, which say, that it must be so?
26.55: The same hour sayde Jesus to the multitude, Ye be come out as it were against a thief, with swordes and staves to take mee: I sat daily teaching in the Temple among you, and yee took me not.
26.56: But all this was done, that the Scriptures of the Prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled.
26.57: And they took Jesus, and led him to Caiaphas the hie Priest, where the Scribes and the Elders were assembled.
26.58: And Peter followed him a far off unto the hie Priestes hall, and went in, and sat with the servants to see the end.
26.59: Now the chief Priestes and the Elders, and all the whole council sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death.
26.60: But they found none, and though many false witnesses came, yet found they none: but at the last came two false witnesses,
26.61: And said, This man said, I can destroie the Temple of God, and build it in three daies.
26.62: Then the chief Priest arose, and sayde to him, Answerest thou nothing? What is the matter that these men witness against thee?
26.63: But Jesus held his peace. Then the chief Priest answered, and said to him, I charge thee swear unto us by the living God, to tell us, If thou be that Christ the Sonne of God, or no.
26.64: Jesus said to him, Thou hast said it: nevertheless I say unto you, hereafter shall ye see the Sonne of man, sitting at the right hand of the power of God, and come in the cloudes of the heaven.
26.65: Then the hie Priest rent his clothes, saying, Hee hath blasphemed, what have wee any more need of witnesses? behold: now yee have heard his blasphemie.
26.66: What think yee? They answered, and said, He is guiltie of death.
26.67: Then spet they in his face, and buffeted him, and other smote him with roddes,
26.68: Saying, Prophecie to us, O Christ, Who is he that smote thee?
26.69: Peter sat without in the hall, and a maid came to him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galile:
26.70: But hee denied before them all, saying, I wot not what thou saiest.
26.71: And when hee went out into the porch, another maid saw him, and sayde unto them that were there, This man was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
26.72: And again he denied with an othe, saying, I know not the man.
26.73: So after a while, came unto him they that stood by, and sayde unto Peter, Surely thou art also one of them: for even thy speache bewraieth thee.
26.74: Then began hee to curse himself, and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.
26.75: Then Peter remembred the wordes of Jesus, which had sayde unto him, Before the cock crow thou shalt denie me thrise. So he went out, and wept bitterly.

27.1: When the morning was come, all the chief Priests, and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, to put him to death,
27.2: And led him away bound, and delivered him unto Pontius Pilate the gouernour.
27.3: Then when Judas which betraied him, saw that hee was condemned, hee repented himself, and brought again the thirtie pieces of silver to the chief Priestes, and Elders,
27.4: Saying, I have sinned, betraying the innocent bloud. But they sayde, What is that to us? see thou to it.
27.5: And when hee had cast down the silver pieces in the Temple, hee departed, and went, and hanged himself.
27.6: And the chief Priestes took the silver pieces, and sayde, It is not lawful for us to put them into the treasure, because it is the price of bloud.
27.7: And they took counsel, and bought with them a potters field, for the burial of strangers.
27.8: Wherefore that field is called, The field of bloud, until this day.
27.9: (Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the Prophet, saying, And they took thirtie silver pieces, ye price of him that was valued, whom they of ye children of Israel valued.
27.10: And they gave them for the potters field, as the Lord appointed me.)
27.11: And Jesus stood before ye gouernour, and the gouernour asked him, saying, Art thou that King of the Iewes? Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest it.
27.12: And when he was accused of the chief Priestes, and Elders, he answered nothing.
27.13: Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they lay against thee?
27.14: But he answered him not to one word, in so much that the gouernour marueiled greatly.
27.15: Now at the feast, the gouernour was wont to deliver unto the people a prisoner whom they would.
27.16: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
27.17: When they were then gathered together, Pilate said unto the, Whether will ye that I let loose unto you Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?
27.18: (For he knew well, that for enuie they had delivered him.
27.19: Also when he was set down upon the iudgement seat, his wife sent to him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream by reason of him.)
27.20: But the chief Priestes and the Elders had persuaded the people that they should ask Barabbas, and should destroy Jesus.
27.21: Then the gouernour answered, and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I let loose unto you? And they said, Barabbas.
27.22: Pilate said unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus, which is called Christ? They all said to him, Let him be crucified.
27.23: Then said the gouernour, But what evil hath he done? Then they cryed the more, saying, Let him be crucified.
27.24: When Pilate saw that he auailed nothing, but that more tumult was made, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just man: look you to it.
27.25: Then answered all the people, and said, His bloud be on us, and on our children.
27.26: Thus let he Barabbas loose unto them, and scourged Jesus, and delivered him to be crucified.
27.27: Then the souldiers of the gouernour took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered about him the whole band,
27.28: And they stripped him, and put about him a skarlet robe,
27.29: And platted a crown of thornes, and put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand, and bowed their knees before him, and mocked him, saying, God save thee King of the Iewes,
27.30: And spitted upon him, and took a reed, and smote him on the head.
27.31: Thus when they had mocked him, they took the robe from him, and put his own rayment on him, and led him away to crucifie him.
27.32: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, named Simon: him they compelled to bear his cross.
27.33: And when they came unto the place called Golgotha, (that is to say, the place of dead mens skulles)
27.34: They gave him vineger to drink, mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink.
27.35: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, and did cast lottes, that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken by the Prophet, They deuided my garments among them, and upon my vesture did cast lottes.
27.36: And they sat, and watched him there.
27.37: They set up also over his head his cause written, THIS IS IESVS THE KING OF THE IEVVES.
27.38: And there were two theeues crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.
27.39: And they that passed by, reviled him, wagging their heades,
27.40: And saying, Thou that destroyest ye Temple, and buildest it in three dayes, save thy self: if thou be ye Sonne of God, come down from ye cross.
27.41: Likewise also the hie Priests mocking him, with the Scribes, and Elders, and Pharises, said,
27.42: He saved others, but he cannot save him self: if he be ye King of Israel, let him now come down from ye cross, and we will beleeue in him.
27.43: He trusted in God, let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Sonne of God.
27.44: The self same thing also ye theeues which were crucified with him, cast in his teeth.
27.45: Now from ye sixt hour was there darkenesse over all the land, unto the ninth hour.
27.46: And about ye ninth hour Jesus cryed with a loud voyce, saying, Eli, Eli, lamasabachthani? that is, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
27.47: And some of them that stood there, when they heard it, said, This man calleth Elias.
27.48: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spondge, and filled it with vineger, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.
27.49: Other said, Let be: let us see, if Elias wil come and save him.
27.50: Then Jesus cryed again with a loud voyce, and yeelded up the ghost.
27.51: And behold, the vayle of the Temple was rent in twain, from the top to the bottom, and the earth did quake, and the stones were cloue.
27.52: And the graves did open themselves, and many bodies of the Saintes, which slept, arose,
27.53: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy citie, and appeared unto many.
27.54: When the Centurion, and they that were with him watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and the thinges that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truely this was the Sonne of God.
27.55: And many women were there, beholding him a far off, which had folowed Jesus from Galile, ministring unto him.
27.56: Among whom was Marie Magdalene, and Marie the mother of James, and Joses, and the mother of Zebedeus sonnes.
27.57: And when the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathea, named Joseph, who had also himself been Jesus disciple.
27.58: He went to Pilate, and asked ye body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded ye body to be delivered.
27.59: So Joseph took the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
27.60: And put it in his new tomb, which he had hewen out in a rock, and rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.
27.61: And there was Marie Magdalene, and the other Marie sitting over against the sepulchre.
27.62: Now the next day that followed the Preparation of the Sabbath, the hie Priestes and Pharises assembled to Pilate,
27.63: And said, Syr, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, Within three dayes I will rise.
27.64: Command therefore, that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so shall the last errour be worse then the first.
27.65: Then Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: goe, and make it sure as ye know.
27.66: And they went, and made the sepulchre sure with the watch, and sealed the stone.

28.1: Now in the end of the Sabbath, when the first day of ye week began to dawn, Marie Magdalene, and the other Marie came to see the sepulchre,
28.2: And behold, there was a great earthquake: for the Angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.
28.3: And his countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow.
28.4: And for fear of him, the keepers were astonied, and became as dead men.
28.5: But the Angel answered, and said to the women, Fear ye not: for I know that ye seek Jesus which was crucified:
28.6: He is not here, for he is risen; as he said: come, see the place where the Lord was laid,
28.7: And go quickly, and tel his disciples that he is risen from ye dead: and behold, he goeth before you into Galile: there ye shall see him: loe, I have told you.
28.8: So they departed quickly from the sepulchre, with fear and great ioye, and did runne to bring his disciples word.
28.9: And as they wet to tel his disciples, behold, Jesus also met the, saying, God save you. And they came, and took him by the feet, and worshipped him.
28.10: Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid. Goe, and tell my brethren, that they goe into Galile, and there shall they see me.
28.11: Now when they were gone, behold, some of the watch came into the citie, and shewed unto the hie Priestes all ye things that were done.
28.12: And they gathered them together with the Elders, and took counsel, and gave large money unto the souldiers,
28.13: Saying, Say, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
28.14: And if this matter come before the gouernour to be heard, we will perswade him, and so use the matter that you shall not need to care.
28.15: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is noysed among the Iewes unto this day.
28.16: Then ye eleven disciples wet into Galile, into a mountain, where Jesus had appointed the.
28.17: And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some douted.
28.18: And Jesus came, and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me, in heaven, and in earth.
28.19: Go therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the Name of the Father, and the Sonne, and the holy Ghost,
28.20: Teaching them to observe all things, whatsoever I have commanded you: and lo, I am with you alway, until the end of the world, Amen.

Which Christ is also the son of Abraham.

Of the ancestors of whom Christ came.

40:1:17: All those which are reckoned up in this pedigree of David’s stock, as they begat one another orderly in their degrees.

40:1:20: Of the mother’s substance by the holy Ghost.
Which was promised, and made sure to thee to be thy wife.
Receive her at her parents’ and kinsfolk’s hands.

40:2:3: Was much moved, for he was a stranger, and came to the kingdom by force: and the Jews were troubled: for wickedness is mad and raging.
40:2:4: The chief priests, that is, such as were of Aaron’s family, which were divided into four and twenty orders, 1 Chron. 14:5 and 2 Chron. 36:14.

That shall rule and govern: for Kings are fitly called leaders and shepherds of the people.

The rich and costly presents, which they brought him.

40:2:13: Christ being yet scarce born, beginneth to be crucified for us, both in himself, and also in his members.
40:2:17: For God speaketh by the mouth of the Prophets.
40:2:18: A voice of lamenting, weeping, and howling.

That is to say, All that compass about Bethlehem: for Rachel Jacob’s wife, who died in childbirth, was buried in the way that leadeth to this town, which is also called Ephrathah, because of the fruitfulness of the soil, and plenty of corn.

40:3:1: In a hilly country, which was notwithstanding inhabited, for Zechariah dwelt there, Luke 1:40, and there was Joab’s house, 1 Kings 2:34; and besides these, Joshua maketh mention of six towns that were in the wilderness, Josh. 15:62.

Not when Joseph went to dwell at Nazareth, but a great while after, about the space of 15 years: for in the 30 year of his age was Jesus baptized of John: therefore by those days is meant, at that time that Jesus remained as yet an inhabitant of the town of Nazareth.

40:3:12: Will cleanse it thoroughly, and make a full riddance.
The triumphs of the wicked shall end in everlasting torment.

The Greek word betokeneth a thing of great account, and such as highly pleaseth a man. So then the Father saith, that Christ only is the man whom when he beholdeth, look what opinion he had conceived of us, he layeth it clean aside.

40:4:5: The battlement wherewith the flat roof of the temple was compassed about, that no man might fall down: as was appointed by the Law, Deut. 22:8.
40:4:7: Word for word, Thou shalt not go on still in tempting.

40:4:13: Which was a town a great deal more famous than Nazareth was.
40:4:15: Of Tiberias, or because that country bended toward Tyre, which standeth upon the sea that cutteth the midst of the world.
So called, because it bordered upon Tyre and Sidon, and because Solomon gave the king of Tyre twenty cities in that quarter, 1 Kings 9:11.
40:4:18: Christ thinking by time, that he should at length depart from us, even at the beginning of his preaching getteth him disciples after an heavenly sort, men indeed poor, and utterly unlearned, and therefore such as might be least suspected witnesses of the truth of those things which they heard and saw.
40:4:23: Diseases of all kinds, but not every one: that is, as we say, some of every one.

40:4:24: Weak and feeble men, who have the parts of their body loosed, and so weakened, that they are neither able to gather them up together, nor put them out as they would.

Which at every full Moon, or other changes of the Moon, are shrewdly troubled and diseased.
40:5:2: Christ teacheth that the greatest joy and felicity is not in the commodities and pleasures of this life, but is laid up in heaven for them that willingly rest in the good will and pleasure of God, and endeavor to profit all men, although they be cruelly vexed, and troubled of the worldlings, because they will not fashion themselves to their manners.

40:26:37: The word which he useth, signifieth great sorrow, and marvelous and deadly grief: which thing, as it betokeneth the truth of man’s nature, which shunneth death as a thing that entered in against nature, so it showeth that though Christ were void of sin, yet he sustained this horrible punishment, because he felt the wrath of God kindled against us for sins, which he revenged and punished in his person.
40:26:38: Christ a true man, going about to suffer the punishment which was due unto us, for forsaking of God is forsaken of his own: he hath a terrible conflict with the horror and fear of the curse of God: out of which he escaping as a conqueror, causeth us not to be afraid anymore of death.
40:26:39: Let it pass me, and not touch me.
That is, which is at hand, and is offered and prepared for me: a kind of speech which the Hebrews use, for the wrath of God, and the punishment he sendeth. See also Matt. 20:22.
40:26:40: An example of the carelessness of man.

40:26:50: Christ reprehendeth Judas tauntingly, and rebuketh him sharply, for he knew well enough for what cause he came.
Christ is taken that we might be delivered.

Our vocation must be the rule of our zeal.

From Annas to Caiaphas, before whom the multitude was assembled, John 18:13.

Clouds of heaven, see also Matt. 24:30.
